name: Just-get-a-job theory

card.summary: The just-get-a-job theory is a looksmax.org framework holding that steady work and income raise perceived status and open up social circles and dating, supplementing or substituting for appearance.
card.note: A forum meme-framework; the same community also posts a joking 'no job theory' variant.

quick.overview:
The just-get-a-job theory is a community claim that employment and income improve one's dating and social prospects regardless of face or build. Proponents argue that money pays for surgery, grooming and style, that a job raises perceived status, and that work puts people into social contact.

It belongs to a family of 'just X theory' forum posts (just approach, just get braces, just be her type) that are partly tongue-in-cheek. No published study tests the theory under this name, though research on income, status and mate preference is a broader field.
quick.how: In practice the theory is a way of framing priorities: finish school, take a job, use income to fund appearance improvements and social life, and meet people through the workplace. Posters describe it as reintroducing them to a social circle.
quick.risks: It is an opinion thread, not a protocol, and carries no physical risk. A joke variant, 'no job theory', describes unemployment as an advantage with married women; it is presented as a meme and has no supporting evidence.

lead: The just-get-a-job theory is one of many 'just X theory' threads on looksmax.org, a framework claiming that having a job and income matters for dating and social success alongside, or beyond, physical appearance.[1]

One thread, titled as a 'LifeFuel', argues that money underlies every 'lifemaxx', from surgery to dating, and that a job brings perceived status, wealth and a social circle, noting that many people meet partners through work.[1] Replies in the same thread parody the format with alternatives such as 'just approach', 'just get braces' and 'just be her type'.[1]
A separate thread, 'no job theory', inverts the idea in a joking, sexual register; other users challenged its basis.[2] No peer-reviewed research tests the theory by name.

chain: Money for grooming, style, surgery; higher perceived status; work social contacts
angle.text: Proponents say a job raises perceived status and funds appearance improvements, and that workplaces are where many people meet partners.

infobox: Employment and income support dating prospects
Just approach, just get braces, no job theory

paras: The theory is stated in a thread whose original poster says that after finishing school a job reintroduces a person to their social circle, and that money covers 'every lifemaxx conceivable'.[1] A reply summarises the mechanism as higher perceived social status, increased wealth, and the many couples who meet through work.[1]

The theory is one of a series of 'just X theory' posts in which users propose single explanations for dating success, and replies often answer with rival theories, some ironic. One reply argues that being 'her type' is the only legitimate theory.[1] A separate thread, 'no job theory is legit for pulling married females', claims the opposite for a niche scenario; a reply asked what it was based on.[2]

lore.intro: The theory circulates as a half-serious post format on looksmax.org.[1]

claims.claim: A job and income improve dating and social outcomes
claims.believers: Posters say money funds surgery and grooming, raises perceived status, and workplaces supply partners.[1]
claims.experts: No published study has tested this framework by name.

claims.claim: 'No job theory' helps with married women
claims.believers: The original poster claims unemployed men can meet stay-at-home wives during the day.[2]
claims.experts: No research supports this; other users in the thread asked what it was based on.[2]
